ddl:
CREATE TABLE Customer (
    Creation_Time DATETIME,
    Customer_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    Deletion_Time DATETIME,
    Email VARCHAR(255),
    Name VARCHAR(255),
    Update_Time DATETIME
);

CREATE TABLE User (
    Creation_Time DATETIME,
    Deletion_Time DATETIME,
    Email VARCHAR(255),
    Password VARCHAR(255),
    Update_Time DATETIME,
    User_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    Username VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Order (
    Creation_Time DATETIME,
    Creator_User_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    Currency_Type VARCHAR(255),
    Customer_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    Deletion_Time DATETIME,
    Delivery_Date DATETIME,
    Invoice_Number VARCHAR(255),
    Order_Description VARCHAR(255),
    Order_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    Order_Number VARCHAR(255),
    Update_Time DATETIME,
    FOREIGN KEY (Creator_User_ID) REFERENCES User(User_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Customer_ID) REFERENCES Customer(Customer_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE Quotation (
    Creation_Time DATETIME,
    Creator_User_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    Customer_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    Deletion_Time DATETIME,
    Description VARCHAR(255),
    Quotation_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    Quotation_Number VARCHAR(255),
    Update_Time DATETIME,
    FOREIGN KEY (Creator_User_ID) REFERENCES User(User_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Customer_ID) REFERENCES Customer(Customer_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE Order_Item (
    Creation_Time DATETIME,
    Deletion_Time DATETIME,
    Description VARCHAR(255),
    Order_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    Order_Item_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    Quantity INTEGER,
    Unit VARCHAR(255),
    Unit_Price FLOAT,
    Update_Time DATETIME,
    FOREIGN KEY (Order_ID) REFERENCES Order(Order_ID)
);

The following is the database requirements analysis for the customer order management system: The system involves the management of customers, orders, order items, and quotations, including the roles of users in customer order creation and quotation.

First, there is the customer (Customer ID, Creation Time, Update Time, Deletion Time, Email, Name) entity, which records the detailed information of the customer. Customer ID serves as the Primary key, while Email and Name serve as the basic contact information of the customer. The customer table ensures that each customer's record is complete, including the creation, update, and deletion times of the customer.

The order (Order ID, Creation Time, Update Time, Deletion Time, Order Description, Delivery Date, Invoice Number, Currency Type, Order Number, Creator User ID, Customer ID) entity records the detailed information of the order. Each order is identified by the Order ID as the Primary key, and the Creator User ID and Customer ID are associated with the user table and customer table, ensuring the relationship between the order creator and the customer. The order table also records important information such as the delivery date and invoice number of the order.

The order item (Order Item ID, Creation Time, Update Time, Deletion Time, Description, Quantity, Unit, Unit Price, Order ID) entity records the specific items under each order, and each order can contain multiple order items. The order item is associated with the order table through a Foreign key, ensuring that each order item belongs to a specific order.

The user (User ID, Creation Time, Update Time, Deletion Time, Email, Username, Password) entity records all user information in the system, including the basic information and authentication information of the user. The user table is the creator of orders and quotations, managing the interaction between customers and orders.

In addition, the user creates orders for customers (Order ID, Customer ID) relationship table represents the many-to-many relationship between users and customers. A user can create multiple orders for a customer, and each customer can also have orders created by multiple users.

The order items of an order (Order Item ID, Order ID) relationship table is used to record the multiple order items contained in each order, ensuring that each order item is associated with a specific order in the order table.

The user quotes for customers (Quotation ID, Customer ID) relationship table records the quotation information provided by users to customers, representing the many-to-many relationship between users and customers.

These designs ensure that the system can effectively manage the relationships between customers, orders, order items, and quotations, and support the role of users in the order creation and quotation process.

The database schema named 'rschema_0100' contains five tables: Customer, User, Order, Quotation, and Order_Item.
The Customer table is used to store customer-related information. It includes columns for Creation_Time, Customer_ID (which is the primary key), Deletion_Time, Email, Name, and Update_Time. All columns allow null values.
The User table stores user-related information. It includes columns for Creation_Time, Deletion_Time, Email, Password, Update_Time, User_ID (the primary key), and Username. All columns allow null values.
The Order table contains information about orders. It includes columns for Creation_Time, Creator_User_ID (which is a foreign key referencing the User table), Currency_Type, Customer_ID (a foreign key referencing the Customer table), Deletion_Time, Delivery_Date, Invoice_Number, Order_Description, Order_ID (the primary key), Order_Number, and Update_Time. All columns allow null values.
The Quotation table contains information about quotations. It includes columns for Creation_Time, Creator_User_ID (a foreign key referencing the User table), Customer_ID (a foreign key referencing the Customer table), Deletion_Time, Description, Quotation_ID (the primary key), Quotation_Number, and Update_Time. All columns allow null values.
Finally, the Order_Item table contains information about the items in orders. It includes columns for Creation_Time, Deletion_Time, Description, Order_ID (a foreign key referencing the Order table), Order_Item_ID (the primary key), Quantity, Unit, Unit_Price, and Update_Time. All columns allow null values.
This schema ensures that the data integrity of the database is maintained by enforcing primary and foreign key constraints, and by allowing null values in all columns. It also ensures referential integrity by ensuring that the foreign keys in the Order, Quotation, and Order_Item tables reference the primary keys in the User and Customer tables.
